All respondents agree that the majority of the girls or young women in this community belong to third step in as far as power and freedom to make decisions is concerned. This means that the majority of the young women have power and freedom to make some major life decisions.
Our parents have full power and freedom to make most of the major decisions. I can make decisions in case my parents are away and I am left with my young brothers and sisters.
[Another one?] We depend on parents to decide. What we can do is to suggest to them and if our ideas seem reasonable, they will work on them.
For one to make all decisions is when you have your household and you are the household head there.
By going to school we get to understand how to read and write.
Going to school we get to know new languages such as Kiswahili and English.
[Is it useful to get an education?] Educated people are able to assist their family members and people around them get ahead.
If one studies to the university level, he or she will be able to teach other people in the community.
We cannot have hospitals without people getting educated.
With education we get to understand better the environment surrounding us.
With education we are able to get the agricultural extension officers.
Good leaders are people who have studied to high levels.
All respondents get to an agreement that the majority of the boys and girls in this community normally study to Form IV.
All respondents agree that boys and girls in this community should at least study to the university level.
[Why?] At the university level one can get employed either as a teacher or a nurse.
[Another one?] If you study to the University level it means that you understand many things not like a person who ends at Standard seven or Form IV.

Some parents think that by educating girls they are wasting their money as the girls at the end of the day get married before completing their studies. Other parents however consider education as being important to both their daughters and sons.
Most of the parents would like to see all their children going to school although some still believe that only boys should have education.

All respondents agree that women in this community walk comfortably to the local market.
The married women walk freely to the local market as long as they have good reasons that make them move there.
As long as they are going to get the household needs, the married women are free to walk to the market.

Some of the married women will walk freely while some will not depending on the set up of their relationships. Some husbands never allow their young married to walk in public places. They would rather send other household members to go and do this rather than their married wives going there.
All respondents agree that it is easy for a woman to sell in the local market although the village lacks a local market.
[What makes this easy yet there is no local market in this community?] We have some women here attending shops at XX centre from this community.
In this community we have no specific local market unless when you talk of XX town.
It would be easy local for them to sell in the local market if at all the local market was here in the village.
We have women selling in shops. There is nothing that prevents women from going selling in the market.
If the woman has the capital to open the business in the local market, she has freedom to do this.
